normalization.role: Real four shear-relative sectors and two annuli; CI/n retained in statistics
normalization.caption: Supplementary Fig. 9 | Shear-relative moisture and circulation before paired departures. a,b, Temporary-minus-final contrasts in 700-hPa specific humidity (g kg⁻¹; a) and cyclonic tangential wind (m s⁻¹; b) in four 90° sectors of the 100–300 and 300–800 km annuli. Colour represents sector means, with separate scales for the two variables. The upward-pointing deep-shear vector  defines downshear above, upshear below and left/right relative to the vector. Each sector is centred on one of these four directions relative to . Sector departures are measured from native-area azimuthal means within 50 km radial bins, separately from seasonal anomalies. Total, azimuthal mean and departure share valid cells; cyclonic wind is positive in both hemispheres. Orientation uses mean pre-event deep shear of at least 2 m s⁻¹. Pre-means require three of the four −24-to−6 h observations, retaining 103 paired cyclones. Table S5g gives all 16 means, 95% percentiles from 2,000 paired-cyclone resamples and counts. Sector comparisons are descriptive. Fig. 5 gives the annular pre-event states and subsequent processes.
